a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is trimethoprim; the closest visible contexts sharing trimethoxybenzyl or trimethoxyphenyl-aminopyrimidine motifs report human absolute oral bioavailability well above 20%: trimetazidine 88.7% (range 30–90%) and R406/fostamatinib ~55% with expected F >50%, plus rapid/highly bioavailable rat exposure.

L6 adds epiroprim, a close 2,4-diaminopyrimidine analog of trimethoprim, with low human hepatic clearance (<20% of liver blood flow; CLhep 3.15 mL/min/kg; low by PBPK); the ~49% contribution of hepatic clearance to human blood clearance reflects low total clearance rather than high first-pass extraction.

Other L6 records are not affirmative low evidence for trimethoprim: trimetrexate values are rat perfused-liver clearances under co-administration conditions, and compound 29's high mouse microsomal clearance is for a structurally distinct piperazine-containing diaminopyrimidine.

The only sub-20% absolute F value in the visible set (C36, 19% in female rats for the distant analog IEG) is outweighed by human/mouse values for that molecule and by closer high-F contexts; it is not affirmative evidence for F <20% in trimethoprim.

evidence_gaps: No direct trimethoprim-specific absolute oral bioavailability or matched oral/IV AUC record is present in the supplied cards.
L6 hepatic-clearance records are for analogs (epiroprim, trimetrexate, compound 29), not trimethoprim itself; species and assay differences limit direct transfer.
No query-specific human first-pass metabolism, gut-wall extraction, efflux, or formulation data are available.
